title: Arizona utility evidence for semiconductor and AI infrastructure power capacity
question: Which utility records show real power capacity for semiconductor and AI infrastructure?
why_it_matters: State-level electricity baselines are useful, but power availability for fabs, suppliers, and compute infrastructure depends on utility planning, interconnection, rates, service territory, and facility load evidence.
current_support: FTFN has EIA Arizona electricity context, ACC utility-regulation and eDocket layers, SRP's named 2025 Integrated System Plan Actions Progress Report, the November 2025 E-67 large-load price plan, and Project Huckleberry: a named Meta Mesa Data Center service project that SRP says is online after initial 69 kV service and a May 2024 230 kV substation and transmission in-service milestone.
missing_evidence: named semiconductor-customer tariff treatment and facilities charges
executed electric-service agreements and service studies
candidate_records: specific ACC utility docket or order
SRP or APS customer-specific service agreement or energization record
semiconductor facility load or service agreement evidence
next_action: Follow the named Meta energization example into disclosed load, tariff, agreement, and operating evidence, and select a semiconductor-customer service record before making TSMC or corridor-wide capacity claims.
notes: Phase 51C adds the first named customer project with in-service and online evidence. The gap remains unresolved because one Meta project does not disclose load or commercial terms and cannot establish service readiness for TSMC, suppliers, future data centers, or the corridor as a whole.
